subject: Post-incident SLA credit — Lyra Systems calculation review
messages:
From: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@lyra-systems.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@lyra-systems.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA credit eligibility for May 14 outage

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the postmortem you shared this morning. We appreciate the timeliness. Per our procurement team, we need a formal statement of whether Lyra is eligible for an SLA service credit for the May 14 incident, and if so a line-item calculation we can attach to our finance ticket.

To help, here are the details our finance team expects: the total affected uptime percentage for our production cluster (we observed ~3.8 hours degraded service between 02:06 and 05:50 PDT), the plan's uptime SLO (99.95%), and the billing period date range. Can you confirm whether Redwood will issue a credit, how it will be calculated, and ETA for the formal credit memo?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement needs the doc by end of week to close the month.

Thanks,
Tom Nguyen
Director of Cloud Ops
Lyra Systems
[Attachment: lyra_incident_log_excerpt.csv (csv, 12KB)]

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA credit eligibility for May 14 outage

Hi Tom — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the logs. We're sorry for the disruption; we take availability seriously. I'm looping in Marcus (billing) and Monica (ops) to validate the final numbers.

Initial read: based on our incident telemetry and the uptime window you provided, Lyra appears eligible for a credit under the production SLA (99.95% monthly uptime). I've attached a draft calculation (sla_calc_lyra.xlsx) that walks through how we get to the proposed credit amount. High-level summary:

- Billing period: 2027-05-01 — 2027-05-31
- SLO: 99.95% (allowed downtime ~21.6 minutes per month)
- Observed downtime / degraded window accounted to Lyra: 3 hours 44 minutes (224 minutes)
- Eligibility band: >99.9% underrun qualifies for proportional credit per contract (section 4.2)
- Draft credit: proportional monthly credit equal to 10% of the monthly committed fee prorated to the duration of impact (see spreadsheet cells).

Next steps: Marcus will confirm exact dollar calculation and whether finance needs any additional paperwork; Monica will confirm the incident window we used matches the one in your logs. We'll produce a formal credit memo and the signed service-credit agreement by Monday EOD if that works.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: sla_calc_lyra.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)]

From: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com

Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: SLA credit eligibility for May 14 outage

Forwarding Tom's note and Laura's draft. Quick internal note before we send the memo: Monica, did ops include the 10-minute suppression window we use for rolling restarts? If we suppress that, the impact drops to 214 minutes, which nudges the prorated percent slightly. Also, legal asked whether we need a standalone signed credit agreement vs. an email acknowledgement — leaning toward a one-page signed memo for our audit trail.

My proposal: use the conservative 224-minute number Tom provided as the baseline for customer-facing calc (matches their logs), then in a separate internal calc show the suppressed number for our internal credits ledger. That avoids back-and-forth and keeps Lyra's procurement happy.

Attached: incident-postmortem-20270514.pdf (ops summary)

Marcus Lin
Billing Manager
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@lyra-systems.com>, Legal Ops <legal@lyra-systems.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, monica_patel@redwoodinference.com, aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Service credit confirmation and issuance — Lyra Systems (May 14 incident)

Tom / Lyra team — thank you for your patience while we validated the numbers. Below is the official confirmation and the next steps to record and apply the credit.

Official determination: Lyra Systems is eligible for a service credit for the May 14, 2027 incident under Section 4.2 of the SLA. We have calculated the credit using the mutually provided incident window (02:06–05:50 PDT) and the billing month May 2027.

Summary of calculation (attached spreadsheet):
- Allowed downtime (99.95% SLO): 21.6 minutes for May 2027
- Observed impact window: 3 hours 44 minutes (224 minutes)
- Exceeding downtime: 202.4 minutes
- Credit band per contract: prorated portion of 10% monthly fee = 10% * (202.4 / 43200) = 0.0469% of monthly committed fee -> rounded credit = $2,130.00 (example — see line-item calc)

What we are attaching and delivering now:
- service-credit-agreement-lyra.pdf (one-page credit memo for signature)
- sla_calc_lyra.xlsx (line-by-line calculation)
- incident-postmortem-20270514.pdf (ops postmortem)

What we need from you: please countersign the attached service-credit-agreement-lyra.pdf and return to legal@redwoodinference.com. Once signed, finance will post the credit to your account and either apply it to next invoice or issue a one-time invoice adjustment per your preference.

Timeline: countersigned agreement expected within 5 business days; credit applied within one billing cycle after signature. If procurement needs a faster internal routing, we can provide an invoice-only adjustment (internal approval required).

If Lyra prefers we put this on a HubSpot-finance ticket, I linked the deal and will update the record when the signed doc comes back: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/LYRA-789234

Apologies again for the incident; we're working on the mitigations listed in the postmortem to reduce recurrence. Please let me know if you want a short sync tomorrow with ops to walk through the postmortem details.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
